subject: Aurora Bank - degraded throughput & 5xx spike (reserved capacity)
messages:
From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aurorabank.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden latency / 5xx spike on reserved capacity - urgent

Hi Logan / Marissa,

We started seeing a spike in tail latency and a burst of 5xx errors against our reserved pool around 07:45 PT this morning. Our home-grown retry logic is firing and customers are seeing timeouts in the payments path. We are on the r-infer-dedicated-16 pool (reservation ID RSRV-aurora-01).

Quick facts:
- Latency p95 jumped from ~80ms to ~1.2s between 07:45–08:00 PT.
- 5xx rate climbed to ~3.8% for that window.
- We are seeing token queueing and a backlog reported in your metrics (attached snippets).

This is an operational customer-impact issue for us. Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal scheduling problem or a noisy neighbor? We need an interim mitigation (fallback model / burst) and a timeline for a permanent fix.

Attached: aurora_error_snippets.txt (excerpted request IDs and timestamps).

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Platform Reliability
Aurora Bank
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aurorabank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 08:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden latency / 5xx spike on reserved capacity - urgent

Hi Marta — thanks for the flag and the snippets. We see the same signal on our side (high queue depth on the r-infer-dedicated-16 pool).

Immediate actions I can take now:
1) Authorize a short-term burst to your dedicated reservation (30 minutes) to smooth the tail.
2) Temporarily route critical payment routes to an identical model in a less-contended pool (no code change required; we can flip at the infra layer).
3) Open an incident channel between your on-call and our infra team (I can start a bridge if you want).

Can you confirm the latest five request IDs in the attached file are the ones you care about? I will copy engineering and ops to validate root cause and push a mitigation.

—Logan
Logan Wright
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora Bank - r-infer-dedicated-16 saturation (customer impact)

Team — customer-reported impact; high priority. Summary below and asks.

Customer: Aurora Bank (DL-8791)
Symptom: p95 latency >1s and 5xx spike ~3.5–4% starting 07:45 PT, sustained for ~20 minutes.
Affected pool: r-infer-dedicated-16 (reservation RSRV-aurora-01)
Customer ask: immediate mitigation + root cause and an action plan to prevent recurrence.

Telemetry (quick): attached grafana link shows queue depth and eviction counts rising; I attached aurora_error_snippets.txt.

Proposed immediate mitigations (please confirm feasibility):
- Naomi: request temporary burst authorization for RSRV-aurora-01 (30–60 minutes) to relieve queueing while we triage.
- David: can you validate whether KV cache pressure / eviction rate spiked for that pool and identify noisy tenants? If so, can we apply per-tenant soft limits or evict aggressively for short term?
- If engineering approves, flip Aurora payment routes to fallback pool (r-infer-hotback-03) until we clear the backlog.

Attachments: temporary_burst_authorization.pdf (I will generate once Naomi confirms), scheduler_patch.diff (suggested scheduler tweak).

This thread will be shared with customer once we have a remediation timeline.
—Logan
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 10:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora Bank - r-infer-dedicated-16 saturation (customer impact)

Logan — quick technical readout from infra:

Root cause signal: a single large tenant (internal ID tenant-7319) ramped an expensive multimodal workload that caused KV cache thrashing and continuous GOP (garbage of old KV pages) evictions. Eviction churn correlates exactly with Aurora's p95 spike window.

Short-term fixes I can do now (30–90 mins):
- Apply an emergency scheduler patch to pin tenant-7319 to a different pool (scheduler_patch.diff attached) — low-risk rolling change.
- Increase aggressive eviction thresholds for r-infer-dedicated-16 for the next 45 minutes to clear the backlog (may increase CPU but will drop tail token latency).
- If permitted, perform a soft restart of the shard manager to flush stuck workers (one shard at a time).

Longer-term mitigation items:
- Enforce per-tenant soft QPS caps for dedicated pools.
- Improve KV cache isolation (work in roadmap Q3).

I will stand by for Naomi's burst authorization and then coordinate the patch window. Metrics + logs: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/aurora/aurora-reserved-capacity?orgId=1#panel=12

—David
David Kim
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@aurorabank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden latency / 5xx spike on reserved capacity - update and next steps

Marta — quick update and next steps after triage: 

What we did (completed):
- Temporary 45-minute burst granted to RSRV-aurora-01; token queue reduced and 5xxs dropped to baseline within ~6 minutes. (attachment: temporary_burst_authorization.pdf)
- Emergency scheduler patch applied to isolate noisy tenant-7319; cache eviction rate returned to normal after rolling restart of two shards.
- We routed critical payment traffic to r-infer-hotback-03 for 20 minutes while the backlog cleared; we reverted the routing once stable.

What we propose next (action items and owners):
- Redwood infra (David): follow up with a post-incident writeup (ETA: 72 hours) including root cause and timeline for KV isolation changes.
- Redwood ops (Naomi / Vivek): propose a standing burst authorization playbook for high-severity customer impacts and provide a one-time credit proposal for the incident (Naomi to own).
- Redwood sales (Marissa): coordinate Aurora's renewal questions and any SLA credit language; Marissa to propose customer-friendly wording.

Customer asks for confirmation:
1) Will Redwood provide a post-incident RCA and a concrete timeline for the KV cache isolation roadmap?
2) Can we confirm next steps on credits / contract language in the next 48 hours?

We will keep this thread as the canonical record. Vivek — looping you for executive sign-off on credits and any customer communication tone.

Thanks for the patience, Marta — we recognize the impact and will make this right.

—Logan
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference
